subtype: Approach: asking a parent to show the right way [Revision]
passage: I'm Irawati. I swept the front room every day and still there was dust in the corners and dirt lines on the floor. I was getting cross. Aaji watched me from her chair for a while. "Beti, come. Let me show you." She took the broom and held it low, pulling the dust in long strokes toward one corner, not flicking it around. Then she held the dustpan flat against the floor. "Slowly. Dust that flies goes back." I tried it, and the pile came together nicely. It took half the time, and my arms were not so tired.

qa.q: How did Aaji hold the broom to pull the dust?
qa.a: Aaji held the broom low, pulling the dust in long strokes toward one corner.

qa.q: What might Irawati be feeling before asking Aaji for help?
qa.a: Irawati was getting cross because the dust stayed even after daily sweeping, and was probably frustrated and tired.

qa.q: What alternative approach could Irawati use, and why?
qa.a: Irawati could watch a neighbour or an older cousin who sweeps well and copy each step. Learning by watching can show details that instructions miss.

qa.q: How might Aaji see teaching Irawati to sweep?
qa.a: Aaji watched from her chair and stepped in kindly, so Aaji probably feels glad to share a skill and happy to see Irawati improve.

grounding: After sweeping badly and leaving dust, a girl asks her grandmother to show the right technique with the corner and dustpan, halving the effort.

passage:
Note for Damini's class teacher, for the Helping at Home sheet
On Thursday Damini swept the verandah by herself. She worked hard, but when she finished there were still grey lines of dust and little heaps she had pushed around. She sat on the step with a sad face and said, "I did it all and it's still dirty." After a minute she came and asked me to show her the proper way. I showed her how to start from the walls and make short strokes toward one corner, keeping the broom low so dust does not fly, then hold the dustpan flat and brush the heap in once. She tried it on the kitchen floor. On Saturday she finished the verandah in half her old time, and it was clean.
- Damini's Dadi, Hansa

qa.q: Where did Damini sweep by herself on Thursday?
qa.a: Damini swept the verandah by herself on Thursday.

qa.q: What was Damini feeling when she sat on the step after sweeping?
qa.a: She felt sad and discouraged, because she had worked hard and still saw grey lines of dust.

qa.q: Which other approach could suit Damini as well, and why?
qa.a: She could break the floor into small sections and finish one at a time, because that shows her which parts are really done.

qa.q: How might the Saturday sweeping look to Dadi Hansa?
qa.a: Dadi sees Damini finish in half the time with a clean floor, and is likely proud that asking for help paid off.

grounding: It shows a girl who still leaves dust after sweeping, asking her grandmother for the right technique and then needing far less effort.

passage:
Sunday
Dear diary, today I swept the whole hall for the pooja guests. It took forever and my arm ached. Then Bhupen walked across in his white socks and held his feet up at me. Grey. I nearly cried. I was so fed up of doing it wrong that I went to the kitchen and asked Ammamma to show me properly. She took the broom and swept in short strokes from the walls into one corner, keeping it low, and then pushed the little heap into the dustpan in one go. "Your turn, good girl, Kiran," she said. I did the bedroom her way. It was done in about half the time and my arm didn't hurt. After lunch Bhupen checked his socks again. White!
- Kiran

qa.q: What colour were Bhupen's socks after Kiran first swept the hall?
How was Kiran feeling when Bhupen held up his grey socks?
qa.a: Kiran felt upset and fed up, close to crying, because all that effort still left the hall dusty.

qa.q: What else could Kiran try next time before starting a big room?
qa.a: Kiran could ask Ammamma to watch the first few strokes, so any mistake is fixed early instead of after the whole hall is done.

qa.q: How might Ammamma see Kiran's request for help?
qa.a: Ammamma probably feels pleased and warm that Kiran came to ask, and enjoys passing on her way of sweeping.

grounding: It shows a girl whose sweeping left dust, asking her grandmother to demonstrate and then finishing with half the effort.
